recl1wvjyRP3XfBBu.Bio: Marty Leeds is a gematria researcher, author and preacher who founded The Gnostic Church and Academy of Lord Jesus Christ in 2022, where he serves as head teacher and spiritual leader. A working minister since 2011, he is the author of more than ten books, among them the Pi & The English Alphabet series, Scripture in the Stars, The Keys to the Tarot and Gnosticism Defined: The Tenets of The Order, built around a mathematical cipher he says is hidden beneath the English alphabet. His teaching centers on Prisca Theologia, the idea of a single wisdom underlying the world's religions, drawing together gematria, Kabbalah, astrology and comparative mythology. He streams weekly sermons free through the Gnostic Academy's YouTube and Rumble channels.
recl1wvjyRP3XfBBu.Name: Marty Leeds

fields.Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "Gnosis Is Experience, Not a Belief System", "body": "Marty Leeds opens by separating historical Gnosticism from gnosis itself, which he defines simply as knowledge of spiritual mysteries received experientially rather than handed down as dogma. He tells Chance Garton that gnosis carries no stipulations and no list of required beliefs, and that it belongs to what he calls the mystery school tradition, the umbrella covering Rosicrucianism, the Knights Templar, Freemasonry and alchemy. Every one of those paths, pursued honestly, leads back to Christ in his view, which is why he named his congregation the Gnostic Church and Academy of Lord Jesus Christ."}, {"title": "Salvation You Cannot Outsource", "body": "Chance Garton presses on the Baptist model he grew up with, where saying the right words in front of a preacher settles your eternity regardless of how you live afterward. Marty Leeds answers that no pastor, priest or preacher makes that determination, that salvation is between you and God, and that it is the same idea other cultures call apotheosis, deification or enlightenment. He frames it as an autodidact hero's journey demanding all of your strength, knowledge and heart. Chance compares outsourced faith to allopathic medicine, an externalized authority people learned over generations to let fix things for them."}, {"title": "Marty Reads Demiurge as Demonic of the People", "body": "The pop culture demiurge, the prison planet and the simulation get dismantled here. Marty Leeds argues the position collapses philosophically, since a malevolent creator made by God pushes the evil back onto God, and since anyone who truly believed the world was a prison would never start a family. Going to the word itself, he reads demiurge as demonic of the people, meaning the world age is built by the evil accepted in the hearts and minds of humans. Chance Garton adds his own objections, including that the doctrine exalts evil far past anything reasonable."}, {"title": "The Devil, Winter and the Natural Order", "body": "Chance Garton traces the consonants of devil to the Hebrew word for world, tuval, and to Tubal Cain the craftsman, arguing the devil figure allegorizes nature's destroying aspect, the winter that makes spring possible. Marty Leeds agrees that world archaically meant the age of man, so the devil ruling this world simply describes what people accept in a given era, from routine circumcision to rampant porn. Neither man accepts that matter is evil. Genesis calls creation good, they note, and sin becomes anything done against the natural order God laid out, which visibly rots and sterilizes."}, {"title": "Nag Hammadi, Eusebius and Suspicious Provenance", "body": "In his closing solo commentary Chance Garton turns to the Nag Hammadi library, thirteen codices supposedly found by a teenage farmer near Nag Hammadi in 1945, and questions the antiquity and the conflicting discovery accounts rather than calling it fake outright. He notes the Codex Alexandrinus enters the record only in the seventeenth century and the Codex Sinaiticus only in 1844. Citing Eusebius on the Egyptian Therapeutae and the Reverend Robert Taylor's commentary, he argues Christianity descends from a much older Alexandrian mystery tradition, and reads the treatise of the great Seth and the teachings of Silvanus as recycled deities."}]
fields.Intro Paragraph 1: Marty Leeds returns to InnerVerse! As the Gnostic Academy's Preacher-Teacher, Marty has been delivering transcendent truths and mathematical mysticism for years, with Biblical analysis that you're not going to find at the average Sunday School. We discuss his new book, Gnosticism Defined: The Tenets of the Order, the Prisca Theologia, and his stance on sin & salvation, misconceptions on the demiurge, symbolism of the serpent, and the origin of evil.
fields.Intro Paragraph 2: In the Plus+ Extension we explore the essential beneficence of the world, the sacrificed savior, a theory on where Judaism began, problems with scapegoating, the world age doctrine, cyclical time, reincarnating world teachers, stellar origins of Islam, the "contact experience," the spiritual place for psychedelics, and much more!

fields.Plus Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "The Lost Sheep and the World as Shepherd", "body": "Part two opens on the parable of the lost sheep, which Marty compares to the Fool of the tarot: everyone arrives on earth without direct answers and needs a guide, even while learning to carry their own life. Chance extends the image to the world itself, noting how dandelions appear where hay fever does, and Marty adds mullein growing at altitude where lungs need help, calling it the logos in creation. Chance then offers his epiphany that whoever leaves the flock to seek the truth gets found by it, which Marty links to the alchemists' magnet stone of truth."}, {"title": "Christ Within and the Real Sacrifice", "body": "Marty argues that Paul taught gnosticism, that the Christ one is told to believe in lives within, and that belief finally means trusting yourself enough to climb the mountain. Chance compares Christ to the trunk of a world tree with each life a branch, equating Christ in you with the pure I am sense of self found in Hindu thought, and he rejects reading the crucifixion as a model of surrendering oneself to the group. Marty answers that sacrifice, like raising a child, returns as benefit and places a divine responsibility on your shoulders, and Chance concludes that the true offering is one's sin, not one's best."}, {"title": "Known by Their Fruits", "body": "Working through the Gospels on Sundays, Marty reads Jesus's rebukes of the scribes and Pharisees as aimed at a specific religious establishment, yet he agrees with Chance that the same words land on any modern pastor, Catholic or Orthodox, who claims sole ownership of the sacred. Chance speculates that Judaism began as something like a reformation of Hinduism and warns that blaming any single group becomes a scapegoat that excuses people from owning what they consume and support. Marty stresses that many decent people get unfairly lumped in, and points to the New Testament's inward definition, a circumcision of the heart, with actions as the only test."}, {"title": "World Ages, Islam and a Text in the Stars", "body": "Chance floats a mystery school idea that a savior figure returns roughly every six hundred years, lining up Moses, Cyrus, Jesus and the rise of Islam as allegory. Marty resists any such dating because the Bible contains no dates and asks why it ignores Brazil or the Maya. He admits knowing little about Islam, but sees the same slide into literalism he faults in modern Christianity, alongside geometric temples, palindromic sayings and a tradition built on the number nineteen, which Chance ties to the moon's nineteen year cycle. Chance relays a friend's view that the constellations themselves are the text, and Marty praises the King James for keeping the numbers."}, {"title": "Contact, the Psyche and Learning to See", "body": "Asked about UFOs and contact experiences, Marty says he has never met anything overtly supernatural and finds such accounts hard to substantiate, while Chance describes watching a luminous orb rise from the ground with two sober witnesses. Chance leans on Jung, picturing the physical world as the densest layer of a shared psyche whose repressed contents burst into view, and Marty recalls Jung reaching a similar conclusion about UFOs. Turning to the tenets, Marty urges balance. He remembers first seeing a letter as a symbol and rows of houses as triangles on squares, and says his mind lit up, fully sober, after decoding Argo Navis."}]
